title: Federal Reserve purse, audit and stopping-power map
adds: The Fed is heavily but not universally audited, and most auditors cannot stop an operation. Stopping power sits with Congress (statute), the full Board (budgets, examination, §248(f)/(h)), each Bank board, the FOMC (open-market domain), Treasury (§13(3) prior approval) and courts; GAO, OIG, outside and general auditors produce evidence another actor must act on. 'Audit access alone is not control.'
